subject: Aurora: operator access, validation package and deployment roadmap
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurorapharm.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aurorapharm.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Aurora: private deployment validation & operator access questions

David —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move towards including Redwood in our procurement packet, the security and engineering teams asked for a tighter description of operator access and the validation artifacts you can provide for an on-prem / VPC deployment. A few specific asks to start with: 

- Operator access model: Do operators require VPN/jump host access? Can operators be restricted to a bastion with MFA? Is there support for time-limited ephemeral access?
- Audit trails: Which kinds of audit logs are produced (auth, admin actions, API tokens, operator console sessions)? What's the retention and export format?
- Offline upgrades & patching: For air-gapped installs, what's the upgrade process and how are signed bundles validated? Do you provide SBOMs and signature manifests?
- Evidence: We need an evidence package (SOC2 artifacts redacted, SBOM, TLS cert handling description, sample network diagram, and a sample operator role matrix).

I'm attaching the RFP question set we use internally (Aurora_RFP_Q1.pdf). We'd like a response by EOD 22 Apr if possible so we can feed answers into the security review next week.

Also include any constraints around egress (outbound telemetry, metrics, auto-update checks) — Aurora's policy is zero outbound connections by default; anything that needs egress will need explicit approval or be routed through an approved jump host.

Liam
Security Engineering
Aurora Pharmaceuticals
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurorapharm.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora: private deployment validation & operator access questions

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear list. We've reviewed the RFP PDF and put together an initial package and a proposed validation roadmap. High-level answers below; I'll attach the detailed operator access whitepaper and a proposed mutual action plan in my next message.

Operator access model:
- Supported patterns: jump-host (recommended), IP-restricted VPN, and bastion with MFA.
- Ephemeral access: yes — we integrate with your existing IdP (SAML/OIDC) to issue time-limited operator sessions and short-lived certificates via our operator auth proxy.
- RBAC: role-based admin separation (cluster-admin, operator, auditor); roles map to fine-grained API scopes.

Audit trails and retention:
- Events logged: auth attempts, admin API calls, operator console sessions (with session start/stop and command-level metadata), model deploy/change events, and KMS key usage records.
- Formats: logs shipped as structured JSON (RFC3339 timestamps) and can be exported to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder or pushed to S3-compatible storage.
- Retention: configurable per-customer; default retention bundle we ship is 365 days but customers can supply their own lifecycle rules.

Offline upgrades & SBOMs:
- Air-gapped upgrades: signed, reproducible bundles (SHA256 + PKCS7 signature). Installer validates bundle signature against customer-provisioned root key (you keep the root offline).
- SBOM: yes, we produce an SPDX v2.2 SBOM for each release and include an integrity manifest.
- Supply-chain: optional reproducible build attestation available on request for regulated workloads.

Egress considerations:
- By default the customer can enforce zero egress. Optional telemetry is configurable; we support routing telemetry via an internal forwarder to your approved destinations or keeping metrics local only.

Attachments in this response: redwood_operator_access_whitepaper.pdf (operator flows, RBAC tables, session TTL examples). We'll also produce a sample network diagram and a sample operator role matrix in the mutual action plan.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical workshop (1.5 hours) with Aurora cloud & security teams — week of Apr 26.
2) Exchange of evidence: we'll push the SOC2 summary, SBOMs, and signed bundle examples to a secured Drive link.
3) Walk through the offline upgrade process in a short recorded demo and live Q&A.

If that timeline works we'll prepare the formal mutual action plan and a proof package by Apr 22; if you need faster, let us know the priority items and we'll accelerate.

Best,
David Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurorapharm.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aurorapharm.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:36:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Aurora: private deployment validation & operator access questions

David —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications we need before the workshop: 

- SBOM required format: must include component hashes and build provenance. Can you confirm SPDX v2.2 + hash for each artifact will be available in the package?
- Signed bundles: Aurora requires that signed bundles be verifiable with a customer-provided public key (we will not ship any key to third parties). Your mention of PKCS7 validation sounds fine; can we get a short sample verification script?
- Audit export cadence: we prefer daily exported bundles to an S3 bucket we control (encrypted with our KMS). Is daily export supported natively?
- Jump host constraints: our policy requires that operators authenticate through an approved bastion and that console sessions be recorded for 30 days and material events forwarded to our SIEM in near-real-time.

I've uploaded our internal access matrix and a short procurement note — Aurora_access_matrix.xlsx — to the drive link in the RFP. If you can include answers inline in the mutual action plan it would help our auditors.

Can Vanessa or Marcus be on the workshop to cover ops/playbook topics? Procurement will push the legal packet after we receive the technical package.

Thanks,
Liam
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurorapharm.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora: private deployment validation & operator access questions

Liam —

Thanks for the notes — Marcus and I will join the workshop. Attached is a draft mutual action plan that maps each of your asks to owners, deliverables, and a proposed timeline. Highlights from the MAP: 

- Deliverables we will provide by Apr 26:
  * Operator access whitepaper (attached previously)
  * Sample network diagram + recommended firewall ACLs
  * SPDX v2.2 SBOM package for the build you saw in the demo
  * Signed bundle verification script (bash + Python examples)
  * SOC2 summary + redacted control evidence (where permitted)

- Aurora responsibilities:
  * Provide the approved bastion/jump host IP ranges and the KMS/public key for signature verification
  * Provision an S3 bucket (or SFTP endpoint) with cross-account role to receive daily audit exports

- Workshop agenda (60–90 mins):
  1) Intro & objectives (10 mins)
  2) Operator access flows & RBAC demo (20 mins)
  3) Offline upgrade walkthrough (15 mins)
  4) Audit/export mechanics + SIEM integration (15 mins)
  5) Q&A & next steps (20 mins)

Attached: mutual_action_plan_AUR-2027-014.docx (contains inline answers mapping to your Aurora_access_matrix.xlsx). Marcus will host the ops portion and run through the verification script.

Proposed workshop slots: Apr 27 (10:00–11:30 ET) or Apr 28 (14:00–15:30 ET). Let us know which works; we'll send a calendar invite and a secured Drive packet with the evidence bundle.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
